```{r setup, include=FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>")
library(CloneCensorWeight)
```

## Disk-backed data tables

`CloneCensorWeightData` follows the FeatureExtraction/CohortMethod contract.
The important tables are:

* `cohorts`: eligible subjects before cloning, then subject-clone follow-up
  with `cloneId`, `arm`, `survivalTime`, `event`, and
  `artificiallyCensored`.
* `outcomes`: subject-level outcome occurrences.
* `covariates`: baseline covariates keyed by subject.
* `covariateRef` and `analysisRef`: covariate metadata tables.

```{r schema}
ccwData <- createSampleCloneCensorWeightData(n = 20, seed = 7)
list(
  cohorts = names(dplyr::collect(ccwData$cohorts)),
  outcomes = names(dplyr::collect(ccwData$outcomes)),
  covariates = names(dplyr::collect(ccwData$covariates)),
  covariateRef = names(dplyr::collect(ccwData$covariateRef)),
  analysisRef = names(dplyr::collect(ccwData$analysisRef))
)
```

## Analysis outputs

```{r outputs}
arms <- list(
  list(arm = "initiate", strategy = "initiate"),
  list(arm = "never", strategy = "never")
)
analysis <- createCloneCensorWeightAnalysis("schema-example", arms, 30)
outputFolder <- tempfile("ccw-schema-")
result <- runCloneCensorWeightAnalyses(ccwData, list(analysis), outputFolder)[[1]]
result$outcomeModel$summary
list.files(outputFolder, recursive = TRUE)
```

The CSV schema is intentionally small and portable: `results.csv` contains
the estimand and confidence interval, while `weightDistribution.csv` records
the cumulative stabilized-weight diagnostics. Large tables remain in the
Andromeda cache and should be loaded with `loadCloneCensorWeightData()` rather
than copied into ordinary R memory.
